'''Adel Javanmard''' (born 1987) is a professor  in the fields of artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics and data science. He has worked on [[high-dimensional statistics]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} IMS Tweedie Award Lecture: Adel Javanmard |url=https://imstat.org/2020/03/31/ims-tweedie-award-lecture-adel-javanmard/ |access-date=2025-09-19 |language=en}}</ref> foundations of [[Deep learning|deep neural network]], [[message passing]], and [[differential privacy]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Publications |url=https://faculty.marshall.usc.edu/Adel-Javanmard/papers_topic.html |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=faculty.marshall.usc.edu |language=en}}</ref> He is a professor of Data Sciences and Operations at the Marshall School of Business at the [[University of Southern California|University of Southern California (USC)]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Adel Javanmard |url=https://www.marshall.usc.edu/personnel/adel-javanmard |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=USC Marshall School of Business |language=en}}</ref> 

== Early life and education ==
While in high school, Javanmard earned a gold medal in the National Mathematical Olympiad in 2003 and a silver medal at the 45th [[International Mathematical Olympiad|International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO)]] in 2004.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=International Mathematical Olympiad |url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=7904 |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=www.imo-official.org}}</ref> He completed his undergraduate studies with BSc degrees in electrical engineering and pure mathematics at [[Sharif University of Technology]].<ref name=":1" /> In 2014, he received his PhD in Electrical Engineering from [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inference and estimation in high-dimensional data analysis |url=https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/10577204 |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=searchworks.stanford.edu}}</ref> His PhD thesis, "''Inference and estimation in high-dimensional data analysis"'' won the Thomas Cover dissertation award from [[IEEE Information Theory Society]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Member profile #9350 {{!}} IEEE Information Theory Society |url=https://www.itsoc.org/profile/9350 |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=www.itsoc.org}}</ref>
== Academic biography ==
After completing his doctorate, Javanmard was an NSF postdoctoral fellow at the Center for Science of Information with UC Berkeley, working with [[David Tse]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Postdocs {{!}} Tse Lab at Stanford University |url=https://tselab.stanford.edu/people/alumni-postdocs/ |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=tselab.stanford.edu}}</ref> In 2015, he joined [[University of Southern California|University of Southern California (USC)]] as a faculty member in the Data Sciences and Operations Department in the Marshall School of Business.<ref name=":2" />

high-dimensional regression |url=http://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume15/javanmard14a/javanmard14a.pdf |journal=The Journal of Machine Learning Research |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=2869–2909}}</ref> robust for Linear Regression |url=https://proceedings.mlr.press/v125/javanmard20a.html |journal=Proceedings of Thirty Third Conference on Learning Theory |language=en |publisher=PMLR |pages=2034–2078}}</ref>
